newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen opening slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen opening slightly higher.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to open a bit higher on Tuesday, adding on to Friday's gains and boosted by activity in AT&T Corp , which is reportedly in merger talks with SBC Communications Corp .
Shares of telecommunications firms were seen supporting the Dow index, after the Wall Street Journal reported AT&T and SBC were discussing a merger deal valued at $50-billion plus.

"We should open today flat to slightly higher after the somewhat unexpected runup on Friday," Peter Carillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments said. Wall Street was closed on Monday for a holiday.

Telecommunications stocks were expected to be very active at the market open on heavy volume, analysts said. Shares of drug manufacturers would also draw attention after news of a large acquisition in Europe, they said.

Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding Ltd announced plans to buy diagnostics and pharmaceuticals company Boehringer Mannheim Group and orthopedics product company DePuy Inc in a deal valued at about $11 billion.
But other analysts cautioned that U.S. stock markets, which rose to record levels on Friday ahead of a holiday weekend, could lose ground at the open.

"I think we will be soft at the open," Joseph Battipaglio, chief investment officer at Gruntal, said. "What we saw on Friday was a lot of portfolio manipulation, a short-term phenomenon. We could give back gains at the start."
On Friday, the Dow industrial average rose 88 points, or 1.2 percent, to close at 7346.
